To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
miR-21 was up-regulated in both head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC), and esophageal squamous cell carcinoma, and that miR- 205 was a marker for squamous epithelial malignancies.
the expression of miR205 is specific to squamous epithelial cells and miR21 is a putative oncogene in HNSCC.
we identified a novel miRNA, miR-205, as a potential marker for HNSCC, and that miR-21 may have a potential role as an oncogenic miRNAs in HNSCC.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the expression of miRNA in squamous epithelial malignancies.
the expression of miRNA in squamous cell carcinomas of the head and neck and esophagus, and the potential use of miRNAs as diagnostic biomarkers.
a comprehensive analysis of miRNA expression in HNSCC, ESCC and other types of cancer.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
miRNAs are not only involved in the development of HNSCC and esophageal cancer but also are potential biomarkers for the detection of these cancers.
miR-21 is a putative oncogene and miR-205 a specific marker miRNAs for both benign and malignant squamous cell carcinoma in human head and neck as well as esophagus.
miR-21 is an oncogenic and miR-205 is a marker miRNA in both normal and neoplastic squamous epithelia.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
miR-21 is a potential oncogenic miRNA for both ESCC and HNSCC, while miR 205 is a specific marker miRNAs for squamous epithelia.

miR-21 and let-7 are the common up-regulated miRNAs in HNSCC, while miR21, miR30a-5P, and miR-16 are the common up regulated miRNAs in ESCC, and miR205 and let- 7 are the common down regulated miRNAs both in HNSCCs and ESCC.
miR-21 is a putative oncogene, miR-205 is an epithelial cell specific marker and miR-16/30a-5ps might be tumor specific marker miRNAs in HNSCC/ESCC.
The main takeaway from our work is that
miRNAs are differentially expressed in normal and cancerous squamous epithelial cells.
miR-21 is a putative oncogene in HNSCC, and miR-205 is a putative tumor suppressor in ESCC.
miR-21 is a promising marker for the detection of HNSCC and esophageal squamous cell carcinoma, and miR-205 could be a specific marker for both normal and malignant human squamous epithelia.
